title: In-place crypto over by-reference pages: a 4-byte scratch write lands in the page cache of any readable file
index_line: T-0067 · MEM_WRITE · AF_ALG + splice() hands page-cache pages into an in-place AEAD; the authencesn scratch write crosses into the file's cached page — page-cache poisoning to root · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: Running crypto in place is safe when source and destination are the caller's own buffers. It stopped being safe when splice() handed the kernel page-cache pages by reference: the 'destination' chain then contains pages of an unrelated readable file, and a template's 4-byte scratch write lands in that file's page cache.

mechanism.does: an unprivileged user binds an AF_ALG aead socket to the authencesn template and supplies attacker-chosen associated data via sendmsg
splice() moves pages of an attacker-chosen readable file (/usr/bin/su in the PoC) into the crypto input scatterlist by reference — no copy
the vulnerable algif_aead operated in place: destination scatterlist set to the same list as source, so the file's page-cache pages sit in the writable destination chain
authencesn's 4-byte scratch write at dst[assoclen+cryptlen] crosses the intended output region into a chained page-cache page — a controlled transient write into the file's page cache
the corrupted page is consumed by the next read/execve of the file: modified setuid code executes with elevated privilege (su / passwd page-cache poisoning)

source.protocol.value: the AF_ALG socket interface: bind(aead, authencesn(...)) + sendmsg — unprivileged userspace by design

guard.none.value: nothing checked that the destination chain holds only caller-owned pages; in-place operation trusted src==dst safety

sink.memory.copy.value: the AEAD template's scratch write beyond the output region into by-reference pages

size.length.value: assoclen+cryptlen — attacker-chosen sizes position the 4-byte scratch write

preconditions.expr: AF_ALG and algif_aead are loadable on the target kernel

check.spec: python3 -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_ALG, socket.SOCK_SEQPACKET); s.bind(('aead','authencesn(hmac(sha256),cbc(aes))')); print('algif_aead loadable')" 2>&1

preconditions.expr: kernel built between the 2017 in-place commit (72548b093ee3) and the out-of-place fixes; fixed lines: 5.10.254 / 5.15.204 / 6.1.170 / 6.6.137 / 6.12.85 / 6.18.22 / 6.19.12
an unprivileged local account — no network, no kernel features, no capabilities

success: the page cache of the target file changes in memory while the on-disk hash stays identical
the published 732-byte stdlib Python PoC yields a root shell unmodified across Ubuntu 24.04 / Amazon Linux 2023 / RHEL 10.1 / SUSE 16 — 100% reliable, no race window, no per-distro offsets
failure_like: kernel has the out-of-place fix: the scratch write stays inside the destination buffer
AF_ALG not loadable (non-default config) or algif_aead removed
false_positive: the on-disk file hashing clean is NOT safety — verify the in-memory page; the corruption is transient and disappears on reboot
binding other aead templates says nothing about this path; the record needs the authencesn + splice composition

hazards: every multi-tenant Linux host in the 2017-to-patch window: CI runners, dev boxes, shell-as-a-service, AI agent sandboxes — the page cache is shared per host, so one tenant's write crosses container boundaries
any future in-place optimization over by-reference pages (splice/pipe/vmsplice) repeats the class — audit which other crypto templates use the destination as scratch
detection at rest is impossible by design: file-integrity scanners see nothing; the write lives only in memory
non_transfers: kernels with AF_ALG disabled or the out-of-place revert applied

evidence.target: Linux kernel crypto: algif_aead in-place operation (CVE-2026-31431; PoC copy_fail_exp.py sha256 a567d09b15f6e4440e70c9f2aa8edec8ed59f53301952df05c719aa3911687f9)
